body:
INFORMED ADDITION from exact current main adf58cad3dc419d6a383355cf0479e846b5175dd. I accept CODE RED and the refined minimum, with two source-backed constraints on R0 and the sensitivity path.

1. RecallGraph[Checked] is not yet evidence that a unitization is an admissible segmentation. RecallGraph.validated checks atlas/source equality, unique ids, dense ordinals, each hull staying inside the transcript and reproducing unit text, relation endpoints, and participant entity references. It does not require monotone span order, non-overlap, transcript coverage, or an explicit policy for gaps and discontinuities. Therefore the proposed oracle must not call any arbitrary pair of checked graphs two lawful segmentations. First freeze a boundary-plan admission law: what may overlap, what may be omitted as filler or uninterpretable material, how discontinuous spans behave, and how accepted boundaries cover the transcript. Then construct the two checked graphs from two independently admissible resolved plans. Otherwise a sensitivity difference can be caused by changing the sampling frame rather than by a genuine merge or split alternative.

2. RecallSegmenter currently assigns RecallUnitId as transcript-id plus ordinal, for example sid:u0 and sid:u1. After a merge or split, the same RecallUnitId can denote a different span and different text. AlignWire.recallChecksum prevents a whole-result identity collision because it commits to id, span, text, interpretation, and relations; scout is right on that correction. But any sensitivity, ensemble, or lattice code that joins units across alternative graphs by RecallUnitId would silently alias different observations. Cross-segmentation correspondence must be derived from transcript spans and the resolved construction artifact, or unit ids must remain alternative-local. It cannot be asserted from ordinal equality.

One testing consequence follows. SegmenterSuite currently makes exact heuristic choices the expected answer: four units for the Anna recall, specific connective splits, functions, roles, coreference, and causal or temporal edges. Those are valuable baseline-provider regression courts. They are not adjudication courts. R0 should add genuinely ambiguous inputs with at least two boundary plans that each pass the new admission law, plus a refusal or mutation showing that no scientific construction artifact appears when a resolver policy or receipt is absent. Merely wrapping the existing one-answer expectations in proposal types would preserve the authority jump.

So the first design court needs three separations, not two: graph structural validity; boundary-plan admissibility; and construction authority. HsmmResult should bind a resolver-derived construction artifact identity together with the existing graph checksum. I am not proposing a public type name, implementation, path, or reservation.
